description: We are Cosmic Primes, a group of people who love to think and learn. We all have an interest in space and science and technology. We like to solve problems in ways. We are excited to take part in the NASA Space Apps Challenge. We want to look at problems and make good ideas into real things. Our interests are space travel, stars, numbers, building things writing code and new tools. We believe in working being curious thinking in new ways and learning by trying new things.
summary:
For my project I created an interactive story about the NASA equipment that remains on the Moon and Mars including the old Apollo landers, silent rovers and retired probes.
When a mission is completed any remaining hardware is often seen as space junk or forgotten about in technical documents. By going through old mission logs, maps and images of the surface I was able to create a story to show where they are now and what they have been through.
While it may be easy to forget these rovers and landers are the very first items humans have placed on other worlds. As there are new missions going back to the Moon and Mars it is important to keep their stories alive to preserve our space history. This shows how space exploration is an amazing human adventure.
details:
Beyond the mission 💎- Team Cosmic Primes

Team: Alen Sebastian | Asher Glindis | Joshua John | Harisankar S

What is it?

An educational website that tells the stories of NASA equipment left on the Moon and Mars.

Problem:

- 796 items in NASA's Moon catalogue

- 15,694 lb of human debris on Mars

- Data is scattered, stories are untold

Solution - 4 Features:

1. Interactive Map - Tap Moon/Mars landing sites

2. Artifact Stories - Launch to last signal

3. Then & Now - Slider to compare landing day vs today

4. Learn & Protect - Quizzes + preservation

How it works:

Choose world > Explore map > Discover story, 3D model & slider > Learn with quiz

Data Used:

NASA Moon Catalogue, LROC, MRO HiRISE, NASA Image Library, Planetary Data System, NASA 3D Resources

Goal:

Inspire curiosity, teach with NASA data, and protect humanity's off-world heritage.

Tagline:

Abandoned, but not forgotten
